architecture_decisions: The proposed architecture decision is to implement a recovery path for the Repository Authorization Required error in the Compact Parallax implementation. This will involve creating a new endpoint for requesting a short-lived provider consent URL for the Project's exact canonical GitHub repository, complete explicit authorization in the provider UI, and then retry the same durable Engineering Run.
work_items: Create a new endpoint for requesting a short-lived provider consent URL for the Project's exact canonical GitHub repository. Complete explicit authorization in the provider UI. Then retry the same durable Engineering Run.
validations: The proposed validation is to ensure that the new endpoint is correctly implemented and that the provider consent URL is returned as expected. The client should be able to request a short-lived provider consent URL for the Project's exact canonical GitHub repository, complete explicit authorization in the provider UI, and then retry the same durable Engineering Run.
AC-01: validate protected requirement — Only an authenticated owner can initiate repository authorization for a Project, and repository identity is resolved only from the canonical Project binding.

AC-02: validate protected requirement — The service always uses the released server-owned GitHub connector and the exact existing `github_app_installation` authorization detail for one canonical repository and fixed delivery permissions. Client input cannot alter these values.
AC-03: validate protected requirement — Authorization initiation uses request/deployment-scoped Vercel OIDC and introduces no PAT, reusable personal token, user credential, or stored provider bearer.

AC-04: validate protected requirement — The server calls only the fixed Connect authorization endpoint with bounded timeout and no redirect following. Provider timeout, transport error, non-2xx, malformed body or missing fields fail closed.

AC-05: validate protected requirement — Only a bounded HTTPS authorization URL on the explicit provider allowlist is returned. Malicious schemes, credentials, unexpected origins, ports, malformed/oversized values and unsafe redirects are rejected.

AC-06: validate protected requirement — The public API returns only status, validated authorization URL and normalized expiry. Provider request/verifier identifiers, raw payloads and tokens are neither returned nor durably stored.

AC-07: validate protected requirement — The autonomous client can distinguish `REPOSITORY_AUTHORIZATION_REQUIRED` through a bounded structured error code without parsing a human message. Generic provider failures do not masquerade as repository consent.

AC-08: validate protected requirement — Authorization initiation does not change Engineering Run state/revision, approved Work Specification, source lineage, provider delivery state, or target repository contents.

AC-09: validate protected requirement — Web and mobile surfaces show an accessible `Authorize repository` action only for the exact authorization-required condition, while preserving the existing saved-progress and same-run `Try again` behavior.

AC-10: validate protected requirement — The client opens only the server-validated authorization URL through the platform external-link mechanism. It does not receive provider bearer tokens or authorization verifier material.

AC-11: validate protected requirement — After a mocked successful provider consent, retrying the same run uses the ordinary exact-repository token request and exact-one-repository GitHub verification before source/provider authority is accepted.

AC-12: validate protected requirement — Canceled, expired, wrong-repository or otherwise incomplete consent does not mark the Project ready; retry returns to the authorization-required boundary without source mutation.

AC-13: validate protected requirement — Existing credential-free public source bootstrap, Python full-experience behavior, OT Time `.NET` source-only acceptance path, validation snapshots, delivery-mode behavior and REVIEW ceiling remain green.

AC-14: validate protected requirement — The change cannot add repository installation coverage silently, select all repositories, grant arbitrary permissions, mutate source before explicit provider consent, merge, deploy production, approve work or complete REVIEW.

AC-15: validate protected requirement — Before semantic release is treated as viable, a non-mutating preview/runtime diagnostic proves the production-style OIDC identity can create an exact-repository Connect authorization request and that the returned URL passes the released safe-origin validator. Diagnostic request/verifier values are not printed and temporary diagnostic code is removed before merge.

AC-16: validate protected requirement — After release and explicit exact-repository provider consent, the existing Decision Ledger trial continues through the normal authenticated path using the same canonical Project/approved specification or a governed exact equivalent, with no out-of-band source edits, and records accepted source, protected validation, Vercel Preview and REVIEW evidence.

AC-17: validate protected requirement — If provider consent or the replay exposes another product boundary, it is recorded honestly and receives separate governance rather than weakening authorization or benchmark gates.

AC-18: validate protected requirement — This exact spec obtains authentic DSPy SpecCritic + SpecCompiler evidence before semantic implementation. Final exact head passes protected spec validation, focused/full tests, client/browser acceptance, Bounded Autonomy, protected promotion evaluation and standard release gates before merge/deployment.

The client should be able to request a short-lived provider consent URL for the Project's exact canonical GitHub repository, complete explicit authorization in the provider UI, and then retry the same durable Engineering Run.
